fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Surfing the Front Edge of the AI Tools", "body": "Thomas Gorence tells Chance Garton he made it his mission this year to learn every new visual AI tool, comparing it to surfing or to the wild west of 1990s computing. He walks through Mid Journey, the Discord bot where a prompt like 1980s sitcom, full house DVD rip, film grain produced the fake retro television stills that fooled viewers into thinking they were real Russian shows. Because the models learned from scraped file names and tags, knowing how to phrase a prompt matters, exactly like knowing how to talk to a brand new search engine."}, {"title": "The Boogeyman Is Dependence, Not Skynet", "body": "Gorence says he does not expect robots to start murdering anyone. His worry is quieter, that we become so reliant on technology that when the people who understand it retire and die, or an EMP wipes the systems, nobody can rebuild what we lost. He compares it to forgetting how the ancients built strong columns, except a microprocessor cannot be reverse engineered without matching technology. He also warns about faulty rules creeping into models the way Rockefeller medicine treats a symptom and leaves you months later wondering why your leg is swollen."}, {"title": "Chance Argues That Logic Is a Light", "body": "Chance Garton offers a counter case. Every doomsday has been a false alarm, so instead of Terminator 2 he frames AI spiritually. Computing runs on logic, and logic is the yang half of yin and yang, the ordering, clarifying, light bringing force. He argues we have been sold the idea that logic is dehumanizing, when logic is what lifts us out of chaos, so a system built on sound logic should produce good, and one built on broken logic will simply self destruct. Gorence pushes back that good logic is as abstract a promise as good communism."}, {"title": "Thirteen Billion Dials and the Inverted Keys", "body": "The most important shift, Gorence argues, is that we inverted our control over technology. Programmers used to write the logic and understand it. Now a trained model has something like thirteen billion little dials, more parameters than any human could hold in mind at once, and we spend our time reverse engineering what it is already doing. AI has taken the car keys. He notes it finds correlations humans would never look for, which is why big data became the currency and why Nvidia stock is shooting through the roof as everyone buys GPUs."}, {"title": "Why the Video Jitters and Hands Got Fixed", "body": "Asked why AI video feels like a string of parallel potentials rather than one fluid recording, Gorence explains stable diffusion. Each frame begins as random static from a seed, then denoises into detail, and settings like previous frame influence, clip skip and CFG control how wild the motion gets. He names Deforum for prompt blending, Runway ML Gen 2 for coherence, and Control Net with Open Pose plus the hand extension, which places a colored stick figure and finger joints so hands are no longer a problem. He also points to Across the Spider Verse."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Thomas Gorence is THE Paranoid American, a conspiratorial media mogul of sorts. In tonight's live episode we will get to know him better, while exploring the efficacy and enjoyability of communicating through the comic book medium. Along the way, we'll dip into dialogue on his innovations with AI art, his experiences and thoughts on Freemasonry, and if he's got any juicy revelations to share about the esoteric knowledge preserved by secret societies.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Society With Secrets", "body": "Gorence has been a Freemason for roughly fifteen years, raised in the Scottish Rite in Orlando after a stranger walked into the Kinko's where he was working a three in the morning shift, recognized his grandfather's ring and started feeding him prompts he had no idea how to answer. His framing of the order is the fraternity's own line back at it: not a secret society but a society with secrets, where the working material is never written down and passes from one man's mouth to another's ear. He reads that as a genuine thread back to the older mystery schools rather than proof of anything sinister."}, {"title": "Wisdom Taught Before Knowledge", "body": "The most durable thing Gorence took out of lodge is that knowledge on its own saves nobody. A person could hold every book in a library in their head and still lack the wisdom, the ethics or the sense of justice to put any of it to use. His reading is that the mystery schools solved this by teaching wisdom first, through analogy and symbol, which is what as above so below is actually unlocking. He compares it to the old aptitude test questions where apple is to banana as potato is to something, a way of thinking you have to derive yourself rather than look up."}, {"title": "The Lodge Is Not Where Power Went", "body": "Asked by Chance whether Masons still run anything, Gorence puts the real leverage in boardrooms, think tanks and intelligence agencies instead. He describes lodges and secret societies generally as prototypal intelligence services from before the OSS and the CIA, useful mainly because they made a clique less personal and let information move between acquaintances who would never otherwise have met. A century ago that mattered, when the FBI had no centralized database and Masonry worked as an open intelligence system. Insurance funds and trade unions commoditized the same idea, and the modern degree system survives as that structure secularized into diplomas and receipts."}, {"title": "A Masonic Council's Forgotten Brain Research", "body": "The research Gorence came to share opens in 1901, when a Japanese chemist first synthesized adrenaline from cattle adrenal glands, the first drug ever sourced from an animal rather than a plant, a seed or bark. Mescaline surfaced in the same period and was found to mimic what physicians then lumped together as dementia praecox. In 1934 the Scottish Rite Supreme Council, Northern Jurisdiction, chose that condition as the single project it would pour its money into, and its presentation that year is among the earliest places adrenochrome is floated as something acting on the mind rather than as a blood coagulant."}, {"title": "Blood Magic as Adrenaline Training", "body": "Gorence's closing thesis reframes ritual bloodletting as physiological conditioning rather than superstition. Adrenaline that goes unburned breaks down into adrenochrome, and patients diagnosed as schizophrenic were measured carrying four to ten times the ordinary amount. His argument is that anyone repeatedly doing something extreme enough to flood their own system is training the body to process that load, the way medieval figures built tolerance by swallowing a little poison each day. He likens it to a gym session for the adrenal system, and notes the same studies put musicians, artists and poets above bankers and accountants."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "If you moved to a new city and you weren't a Freemason, it might be a lot harder to find a job than if you were.", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/fbd719df-0ba7-4156-8bc2-82adb96cb679/PARANOID-AMERICAN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Any power system where there's a differential of power held by a group, there's gonna be opportunity, and that opportunity is gonna be taken for abuses of that power.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's plenty of people that are book smart that are still not wise.", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/fbd719df-0ba7-4156-8bc2-82adb96cb679/PARANOID-AMERICAN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Conspiracy culture does love to make everything the Masons, the Masons, and maybe for good reason.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The number 33 is eventually gonna pop up in just a general game of numbers. It would be even crazier if you just never saw a certain number ever in public.", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/fbd719df-0ba7-4156-8bc2-82adb96cb679/PARANOID-AMERICAN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I would also describe Masonry and almost any other secret society as just prototypal intelligence agencies before the OSS, before the CIA.", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/fbd719df-0ba7-4156-8bc2-82adb96cb679/PARANOID-AMERICAN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I feel like there's morality baked into the universe. There's a moral law in a way, in a cause and effect type of sense.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You can't even say the word adrenochrome without sounding like you're about to start talking about Pizzagate in the very next sentence.", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/fbd719df-0ba7-4156-8bc2-82adb96cb679/PARANOID-AMERICAN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I've heard accounts of people eating the organ of an animal like a rabbit's heart and having dreams of being a rabbit or tunneling underground or things of that nature.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Blood magic and weird rituals, the more you make yourself crazy and come back from that brink of craziness, think of it like you're going to the gym and you're exercising.", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/fbd719df-0ba7-4156-8bc2-82adb96cb679/PARANOID-AMERICAN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "It reminds me of when search engines were brand new and if you knew how to talk to a search engine You were like 10 or 20 times faster than anyone else if you just knew like the tricks and how to speak to it", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "And the ultimately so ultimately what I think is that we've been fed for a long time a bunch of Bs that logic is dangerous that logic taken to its conclusion is like somehow dehumanizing or inhumane", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But even scarier than that and I think the most important point is that with ai we've kind of inverted our control over technology So up until ai starts getting a huge boom over the last decade or so, especially in consumer market", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "Are we on this road of externalizing further and further our capacity to do it ourselves from our own imagination with our own hands and Is that a pendulum that reaches some kind of apex? Is that what the singularity means?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The druids for example, originally they were not interested in keeping their esoteric doctrines In written form because it was important to them for their initiates to actually exercise the capacity of their memory", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "A laura operates by injecting its own biases into the model So if I go and get like a jfk laura And I just type apple if that laura model is strong enough It'll only make apples that look like jfk or jfk eating apples or like every single thing will have jfk in it", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": ""}, {"text": "It's really interesting it's like everyone has these checkpoints in the form of the actual frames drawn in the comic book But the in between the frames the action that animates that takes you from this image to that image We all get to create that in our own imagination in our own minds", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And it's going to be called the homunculus owner's manual and it breaks down the entire concept Of what a homunculus is how to make one what kind of powers they can give you The names of people that have claims to have unearthed this research", "author": "Thomas Gorence", "portrait": ""}]
